findings.status: OPEN (residual, introduced by the N1 base rule, not by the F1/F2/F3 repair)
findings.title: create accepts a configured protected branch name, after which the untampered record can never be removed or merged.
findings.where: packages/mpd-worktree-plugin/src/ops.ts -> createEntry (validates isValidBranch and branchExists only; never config.protectedBranches) vs revalidateRecordedBranch (force-blind protected refusal).
why_it_matters: The public create tool documents `branch` as an override validated by `git check-ref-format --branch`; a repo whose default is `main` has no `dev`/`master` yet, so `createWorktree({name, branch: "dev"})` succeeds and writes a record naming `dev`.

Afterwards revalidateRecordedBranch refuses that record for BOTH remove(force:true) and merge(force:true) with `protected-branch`, so the worktree, its branch and its registered name are stranded: the tool cannot clean it up, and only hand-editing .mpd/worktrees/index.json or changing the config recovers. The branch's commits are not lost, but the workspace cannot be returned to a clean state through the tool.

Probe evidence/worktree/n1-review2/2026-11-12T07-51-14Z/probe-edge.log: `protected=dev create=NO-REFUSAL recorded=dev ... remove(force:true)=protected-branch merge(force:true)=protected-branch recordStatus=active dirExists=true` and the same for master.
This is a legitimate (untampered) create path, so it is distinct from the required tampered-record refusal; the prior N1 pass tested only the default `agent/` branch, so it did not see this state.
findings.direction: Refuse `plan.branch` in `config.protectedBranches` inside createEntry (and the reattach recovery) with a typed refusal, matching the existing force-blind revalidation; alternatively document the bound and provide a sanctioned recovery. Do NOT weaken the recorded-branch refusal.

declinedToJudge: Merge-TARGET protection remains force-bypassable — pre-existing and frozen in .mpd/plans/agent-worktrees.md §3 Lane A; unchanged by this diff.

A vanished-directory remove still deletes an existing UNPROTECTED branch named by the record (no HEAD to interrogate); this is the previous verifier's accepted bound, force-gated and unchanged by the repair.
A consistent path+branch tamper could point a record at another registered worktree of the same repo; N1 names the branch field, path trust is the pre-existing N6 residual.
Validation is check-then-act (TOCTOU); destructive operations consume only the validated branch NAME, so a protected branch cannot be redirected into deletion/merge.
`isValidBranch` uses `git check-ref-format --branch` for its exit code only (it can expand names like `@{-1}`); any expansion still fails branchExists/HEAD equality, so the path is fail-closed.
Case-folding of protected branch names (e.g. MASTER) on case-insensitive filesystems was not exercised on this Linux host.
`createForMember`/`cwdForMember` still return an existing record's branch without revalidation; N1 names remove/merge only and cwd is separately gated by existsSync + isGitManaged.

`merge` of a vanished directory now refuses unregistered-worktree (before N1 it would merge the branch); the task explicitly requires this refusal and all four docs state it, so it is not counted as a regression.

The docs phrase "without a live comparison" is read as "no HEAD comparison": remove still checks branch existence later (and may delete the branch). The same sentence's "cannot answer for HEAD" makes the bound accurate; not counted.
The probe.log line `fatal: Needed a single revision` in section B is git's expected answer to `rev-parse --verify` on the deliberately deleted branch; the check PASSes.
